text:
A new text classifier called fastText matches the accuracy of complex deep learning methods while operating many orders of magnitude faster for training and evaluation [P2_p1_c02]. 

Traditional linear classifiers can struggle with large output spaces where some classes have very few examples [P2_p1_c04]. To solve this, fastText represents sentences as a bag of words and feeds them into a linear model with rank constraints, while also using a bag of n-grams to capture partial local word order [P2_p1_c04][P2_p2_c03]. 

This approach is highly efficient [P2_p2_c03]. Researchers can train fastText on more than one billion words in less than ten minutes using a standard multicore CPU [P2_p1_c02]. It can also classify half a million sentences among 312K classes in less than a minute [P2_p1_c02]. 

In experiments, fastText achieved accuracy that is often on par with deep learning classifiers [P2_p1_c02]. For sentiment analysis, its accuracy is slightly better than character-level convolutional networks, and adding bigram information improves performance by 1-4% [P2_p3_c02]. 

This development matters because it offers a simple, highly efficient baseline for text classification that drastically cuts down processing time without sacrificing accuracy [P2_p1_c02].
